case.title: The Mysterious Dinner
case.introduction: It is a rainy night in the Grand Oak Hotel. A famous chef is found dead in the dining room. One guest is not who he says he is.
case.escape_plan: The killer plans to leave in the hotel lobby at midnight

rooms.name: Dining Room
rooms.description: Long table with candles. The chef lies on the floor.

rooms.name: Kitchen
rooms.description: Busy. Chef used to cook here.

characters.name: Michael Hale
characters.alibi: In the lobby reading a book
lies: He says he is a hotel guest

characters.name: Lisa Grant
characters.secret: She is good at reading faces

characters.name: Dr. Alan Reed
characters.secret: He once treated a famous chef
characters.alibi: In the lounge reading a book

evidence.name: Poisoned Drink
evidence.description: Red wine with a faint smell

hidden_clues: The name Michael Hale is not on hotel records. The real name is Mark Jensen.
red_herrings: The red tie was found in Eve's bag. It does not link to the crime.

solution.reasoning: All key evidence points to Michael Hale, but his name is fake. The real name Mark Jensen is hidden. He used the drink to poison the chef.

state.current_objective: At Grand Oak Hotel tonight, 4 guests are trapped — and one is lying about who they are. Match the clues to the lies and point out the guilty one behind chef death, suspected poisoning. There are many clues to help you.

exchanges.answer: Hey! How's it going? I just finished prep for dessert. Everything's good!

exchanges.question: no the chef is died
exchanges.answer: Oh no! I’m so sorry. I don’t know what happened to the chef. I was in the kitchen making dessert when it happened. I hope the staff is okay.

exchanges.answer: Sure, I can look around. I'll check the kitchen and the back hall. I’ll keep an eye on the dessert station, too. Let me know if you see anything.

exchanges.question: hello i want to ask question again
exchanges.answer: Hi! Sure, go ahead. I’m in the kitchen right now, making dessert. What do you want to know?

exchanges.question: last time you see the chef
exchanges.answer: I saw the chef earlier. He was in the kitchen making dessert, just like me. I laughed when he said the sugar was too sweet. I didn’t see him go anywhere else.

exchanges.question: and which time he come
exchanges.answer: I don’t know the exact time. He was in the kitchen around three in the morning, but I didn’t see him leave until after I finished the desserts.

exchanges.question: and what he making
exchanges.answer: I’m not sure, but he was mixing the sugar and flour for the dessert. I saw him stir it a lot. I didn’t hear anything else.

exchanges.question: and after that where he gone you know
exchanges.answer: I didn’t see him leave the kitchen. He stayed until the desserts were done. After that he just walked out the back door. I didn’t catch where he went next.

exchanges.question: ok thanks
exchanges.answer: You're welcome. Let me know if you need anything else.

exchanges.question: in the morning what you are doing an time
exchanges.answer: I was in the kitchen making dessert. I started around two‑o’clock. I laughed a lot while stirring. I finished by three‑ten, then left the kitchen.

exchanges.question: why you always tidy
exchanges.answer: I always tidy because I like things neat. It keeps the kitchen calm and I don’t feel late. Plus, a tidy space makes it easier to serve guests fast.

exchanges.question: provide me some hint
exchanges.answer: I’m not sure what you need, but if you’re looking for clues, maybe check the back door. The chef left through that way, and I saw him put a weird bottle on the counter before he left. It smelled odd.

exchanges.question: which type of bottle
exchanges.answer: It was a little bottle of wine, I think. I saw it on the counter before he left.

exchanges.question: and which counter
exchanges.answer: It was on the prep counter next to the stove. The little bottle was right there, on the glass table.

exchanges.question: how to you know that was wine
exchanges.answer: I saw it with my own eyes. The bottle had a red label and the smell was like grape juice. I tasted a tiny drop when I was making dessert. That's why I know it was wine.

exchanges.question: you like wine
exchanges.answer: Yeah, I do like wine. It’s good for dessert, and I’ve had it with a few customers before. I just love the taste.

exchanges.question: any time you drink wine with chef
exchanges.answer: I don’t drink wine with anyone. I only serve it to customers. The chef? He’s not my friend. I’m not sure why you ask.

exchanges.question: because in this room we find wine
exchanges.answer: I didn’t bring wine in. I only had the little bottle on the prep counter. It was there before the chef left. I didn’t touch it.

exchanges.question: why you so hasitate
exchanges.answer: I’m not sure. Maybe I’m just worried I’ll be late for work. That’s the only thing that makes me jump.

exchanges.question: anything you want to say to me
exchanges.answer: I don’t have anything else. Just keep asking.

exchanges.question: ok thankyou
exchanges.answer: Thanks. I’m just happy I could help. Let me know if you need anything else. I’ll keep serving the guests on time.
